author: John Stuart Mill
title: On Liberty
edition: Fourth edition (London: Longmans, Green, Reader, and Dyer, 1869). Scan-backed Wikisource transcription. Prose line wrapping is collapsed within retained paragraphs; HTML emphasis becomes plain text. Printed page numbers, navigation, footnote reference markers, and zero-width page-boundary characters are omitted; main-text wording and punctuation are retained. Original verse line breaks are preserved where present. Apparent errors present in the linked transcription are retained rather than silently corrected; this extraction check is not a fresh complete print-image collation. The library text holds the Humboldt epigraph, Mill's dedication and Chapters I to V with their printed titles, ending with THE END; the title page, contents and printer's colophon are omitted; Mill's nine footnotes (five in Chapter II, three in Chapter III, one in Chapter IV) are kept, each anchor as [n] in the transcription's numbering, which restarts in each chapter, and each note as a paragraph [Footnote n: text] after its chapter's text, where the Wikisource transcription lists them. On 2026-11-18 seven further passages (Chapter I from “Like other tyrannies”; the opening of Chapter II; its examples of Socrates, Christ and Marcus Aurelius; its summary of four grounds with the paragraph on temperate discussion; the opening of Chapter III; Chapter IV from “But with regard to the merely contingent”; and the paragraph on contracts, marriage and education in Chapter V) were collated word by word against the OCR of Internet Archive onliberty06millgoog (this fourth edition) and compared with Project Gutenberg 34901, each difference decided on the page images: one reading changed, “not worse than men commonly are” (page 47), where the transcription adds “most”. Later on 2026-11-18 two further passages (the last three paragraphs of Chapter I, and Chapter III from “It is so, on the Calvinistic theory” to “without hindrance”) were collated the same way against onliberty06millgoog and Project Gutenberg 34901: no reading changed.

rights.basis: This original English edition was published in 1869, before 1931, and is public domain in the United States as of 2026. The linked scan index identifies the printed edition; no modern editorial material is supplied.

acquisition.method: Wikisource rendered page HTML (index.php action=render) for the main page and its five chapter subpages in printed order, On Liberty and On Liberty/Chapter 1 to Chapter 5 (revisions 16132207, 3944546, 8111605, 8203199, 8246968, 8253810); downloadSha256 is the SHA-256 of the six responses concatenated in that order and downloadUrl the first of them. Only the transcluded scan text is used, from the epigraph on: Wikisource headers, page-number anchors, and zero-width page-boundary characters removed; centred chapter numbers and titles became headings; paragraphs joined with whitespace collapsed to single spaces and emphasis flattened; footnote calls kept as [n] in Wikisource's per-subpage numbering, attached to the word before them; each subpage's reference list, which the transcription prints after the subpage's text, became one paragraph per note in Project Gutenberg's form [Footnote n: text], its paragraphs and line breaks joined with single spaces (a note that runs on from one scan page to the next is one note, its continuation marker dropped).
